sources.publisher: U.S. House of Representatives, History, Art & Archives
sources.metric: Philadelphia's tenure as interim federal capital
sources.caveat: Philadelphia was the interim capital of the federal government, not the current U.S. capital.

sources.metric: Foreign-born persons and percent of Pennsylvania's total population
sources.caveat: Historical complete-count census. Do not connect directly to modern ACS survey estimates as a seamless annual series; account for changed survey methods, population coverage, geography, and classification. Foreign-born is birthplace/citizenship status, not an annual immigration-flow measure.

sources.metric: Foreign-born persons as percent of Pennsylvania population
sources.caveat: Five-year pooled estimate, not a value for calendar year 2024. Overlapping five-year releases are not independent annual observations. ACS estimates have sampling uncertainty.

sources.metric: Persons age 5+ speaking a language other than English at home
sources.caveat: Home language is not English proficiency, citizenship, or foreign-born status. Universe is age 5 and over. Earlier decennial language questions and categories differ; the modern home-language series starts in 1980.

sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Health, Chronic Disease Burden Report, citing U.S. Census Bureau ACS
sources.metric: Pennsylvania residents age 5+ speaking a language other than English at home
sources.caveat: The report's 2009 and 2019 percentages use the same age-5+ home-language concept. Verify ACS product and margins of error before charting with 2020-2024 five-year QuickFacts.

sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Historical Language Questions
sources.metric: Question wording and universe for language-use measures
sources.caveat: Earlier mother-tongue and childhood-language questions are not the same as language currently spoken at home.

sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Comparing 2020 ACS Data
sources.metric: Comparability warning for 2020 ACS 1-year experimental estimates
sources.caveat: Standard 2020 ACS 1-year estimates were not released. Census says the experimental figures should not be compared with ordinary 1-year ACS, 2020 Census, or earlier censuses.

sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Health, Pennsylvania Vital Statistics 2024
sources.metric: Reported induced abortions: Pennsylvania resident count, resident rate per 1,000 females age 15-44, and occurrences in Pennsylvania
sources.caveat: Table D-1 omits 1976-1979; do not imply a continuous published table from 1975. Resident and occurrence counts differ because of interstate travel. Rate denominator is females age 15-44, not all residents or births. Counts are reports, and reporting/definitions may change over decades.

sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Health, 2024 Abortion Statistics
sources.metric: Induced abortions performed in Pennsylvania, with age, procedure, and residence breakdowns
sources.period: 2024 annual report; department says monitoring began in 1975
sources.caveat: The annual report's headline total is by place of procedure (occurrence), so do not relabel it as abortions among Pennsylvania residents.

sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Health, Pennsylvania Vital Statistics 2024
sources.metric: Pennsylvania resident live births and general fertility rate per 1,000 females age 15-44
sources.caveat: Live births are a different event measure from abortions. The general fertility rate is births per 1,000 females age 15-44, not lifetime total fertility rate.

abortion_resident_rate_pa.unit: reported abortions among Pennsylvania residents per 1,000 females age 15-44

comparability_notes: Do not plot the 1920 census foreign-born share and 2020-2024 ACS share as a continuous measured time series; show separate dated benchmarks.
Do not plot 2009/2019 ACS annual language values in one line with the 2020-2024 ACS five-year pooled value without identifying the change in period.
The Census Bureau did not release standard 2020 ACS 1-year estimates; exclude the experimental 2020 value from ordinary annual trend lines.
The Census Bureau changed detailed language categories in 2016; broad English-only versus language-other-than-English comparisons are safer than detailed-language comparisons across that break.
